title: Connection hold mitigation and smart-retry gentle-shed for tenant surge
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a high-volume tenant surge on 2026-03-09 we observed correlated 5xx spikes and long tail timeouts affecting several customers. Symptoms: edge proxy connection queues exhausted, large numbers of concurrent retries from the SDKs, and eviction churn in the service KV cache. This ticket focuses on a two-pronged short-term + medium-term mitigation: (1) short-term emergency patch to reduce connection hold and stabilize proxy pools and (2) deploy a smart-retry gentle-shed at the frontdoor to prevent retry amplification while we implement longer-term admission control and per-tenant shaping. The scope is Hosted API only for this ticket but the telemetry and patterns will inform Dedicated/Private followups.
updates: 2026-03-10: Initial triage. Pager duty rotation confirmed repeated 5xx waves between 12:14 and 12:46 UTC. Noted spike correlated with a single large customer batch upload. Metrics attached to ticket.

2026-03-10: Reproduced local-ish load on staging using tenant-surge harness; observed connection pool exhaustion in frontdoor proxy (keepalive saturation) and asymmetric retry patterns from SDK clients.

2026-03-11: Short-term patch PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4286 - caps per-tenant concurrent upstream connections at proxy layer and adds 5s aggressive keepalive timeout for idle handoffs. Canary on prod-edge-us-west-2 started.

2026-03-12: Canary showed 37% reduction in queue depth and 22% lower 5xx rate for the impacted tenant during a synthetic surge. Still saw KV cache thrash on backend nodes; opened ENG-711306 (sub-issue) to coordinate KV compaction tuning.

2026-03-12: Added smart-retry gentle-shed shim in SDK gateway: if client-specified idempotency token is missing and tenant is above threshold, respond with 429 + Retry-After to avoid blind retries. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1337. On staging tests passed.
2026-03-13: Rollout to 25% of traffic for low-latency tenants. Observability dashboard (grafana) updated with new panels for per-tenant active upstream connections and SDK retry rates.

2026-03-14: Incident postmortem draft started. Communications prepared for affected customers with mitigation details and recommended SDK upgrade. Engineering review scheduled with Lina Chen and Marcus O'Neal for 2026-03-15.

2026-03-14: Remaining work: enforce idempotency tokens in gateway for safe retries, add per-tenant admission control in routing plane, and KV cache prefetch/compaction adjustments. Estimate updated to reflect additional integration testing.

Review notes: Jon Rivera requested additional unit tests and a load test proof that retry gating does not introduce request starvation for small requests. Aisha approved the initial canary data for emergency patch.
acceptance_criteria: Prod 5xx rate attributable to connection pool exhaustion reduced by >=50% for previously impacted tenants under same synthetic surge profile
Per-tenant upstream concurrent connections capped and visible in dashboard with alerts at threshold
SDK/gateway pair returns 429+Retry-After for non-idempotent requests under shed conditions; no silent amplification observed
No customer-visible increase in end-to-end tail latency outside of the shed window for non-surge tenants
Postmortem completed and customer comms sent to affected accounts
implementation_notes: Edge proxy changes: add configurable per-tenant concurrent_conn_limit (default 200) and lower keepalive_idle_ms to 5000 for handoffs during surge windows
Gateway shim: inspect X-Idempotency-Key or similar header; if absent and tenant_conn_count > soft_threshold, return 429+Retry-After 2s and set x-redwood-gentleshed header
Runtime: add backpressure hook to reject new KV cache writes when mem-pressure>85% to avoid eviction storms; coordinate with ENG-711306
Telemetry: emit tenant.connection_count, tenant.retry_rate, tenant.kvcache_evictions to new grafana dashboard panels and hook to alerting rules
Testing: synthetic tenant-surge harness must simulate realistic SDK retry backoffs (exponential with jitter), large batch uploads, and streaming workloads
rollout_plan: Step 0: Merge emergency proxy patch behind feature flag and deploy to canary edge (us-west-2) - 2026-03-11 done
Step 1: Monitor canary for 24h; if regression-free, roll to 25% of edges and run synthetic surge overnight - 2026-03-12 done
Step 2: Enable smart-retry gentle-shed at 25% and validate customer integration for two pilot tenants - 2026-03-13
Step 3: Full global rollout of proxy caps and gateway shed after 48h stable metrics - target 2026-03-16
Step 4: Post-deploy, enable per-tenant admission control in routing plane (runtime-1.24) and schedule KV compaction tuning in next sprint
testing_plan: Unit tests covering gating behavior and header propagation (sdk & gateway)
Load test: tenant-surge harness with 10k concurrent simulate; measure 95/99/999 latencies and 5xx counts pre/post patch
Chaos test: introduce transient upstream slowness to validate graceful-shed does not amplify retries
Integration test: end-to-end verification with dedicated customer pilot to ensure no request starvation
risks: Overaggressive shedding could cause temporary increased 429s for misconfigured clients — must include clear SDK upgrade path and client guidance
Proxy caps may reveal latent hotspots where a single tenant legitimately needs more connections — will add per-tenant override after review
KV cache backpressure may surface increased cache miss rate and higher cost if not tuned in tandem
Observability gaps remain around long-tail streaming requests; additional tracing required
postmortem_actions: Finalize root cause: connection pool saturation + retry amplification + kvcache eviction loop
Add automated detection for concurrent_conn growth beyond baseline and auto-enable gentle-shed for affected tenant
SDK change: add required idempotency-key warning in telemetry for non-idempotent endpoints
Operational runbook: add step to set proxy feature-flag to limit connections for a tenant and steps to exonerate legitimate high-throughput tenants
Follow-up ticket: ENG-711306 for KV cache compaction tuning and ENG-711307 for admission control rollout
